item.title: The Brand Age, Paul Graham
item.description:
Paul Graham is the co-founder of Y Combinator and one of the great philosophers of the computer science world. For 25 years he has been publishing thoughtful essays on his blog — though infrequently: in 2025, for instance, he published just four pieces. In March 2026 a new one appeared: «The Brand Age». I’d like to discuss it.

Why does this matter to me? Among the writers I follow, Paul Graham comes first. I’ve referenced his essays several times before — in my roundup of resources for product managers, in «The 10 Deadly Sins of a Product Manager», and in «Thinking Through Writing». I’m also drawn to his style: clarifying footnotes and acknowledgments to well-known practitioners who reviewed his drafts. In this latest essay, the reviewers include Sam Altman, among others. And equally important — there’s no advertising, no promotion of any services.

item.title: CEO of the Product: How a Product Manager Creates Meaning and Communicates Value
item.description:
This article was originally published on Delovoy Mir.

Technology today is advancing at an accelerating pace — there’s even a concept called «technological singularity,» suggesting that in some hypothetical future, explosive technological growth will fundamentally transform our civilization.

But it’s worth remembering that technology doesn’t enter our lives on its own. It arrives through IT products, built to solve specific problems or address the needs of a particular audience.

Product managers play one of the central roles in this process. They identify real audience problems, devise the best solutions, create new user habits, shape new markets, and articulate new ideas that will remain relevant in the future.

item.title: Product Management Is Marketing Management
item.description:
And a product manager is a marketing specialist.

This definition is obvious to people who studied marketing in college. But it’s not always clear to those who came to product management from a technical background.

As someone who came up through the technical side, I long believed that «marketing» was limited to finding promotion channels, communicating product value to users, and selling goods — physical or digital, it didn’t matter. But that understanding of marketing is very, very far from the truth.

item.title: Loyalty ≠ Satisfaction
item.description:
Loyalty

Customer Loyalty is devotion to a brand or product. It means that when faced with comparable alternatives, a user will choose our product. This choice is often emotional — a user who loves a product will recommend it to friends and family.

The standard metric for measuring customer loyalty is the NPS (Net Promoter Score), whose growth positively correlates with sales growth and market share gains. This relationship, combined with how easy the metric is to measure, is exactly what made it so popular worldwide. That said, NPS has its fair share of pitfalls — here’s a good article on the topic: «12 подводных камней Net Promoter Score».
